findings.issue_text: [BUG] The conditional-attribute hook is misnamed: ActiveModel::Serializers decides per-attribute inclusion by calling `include_<attr>?`, and this method is `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so the serializer framework never invokes it. `website_name` is serialized unconditionally — every user without a website gets `website_name: null` in the payload instead of the omitted key the guard is written to produce — and the guard is dead code; no test in the diff pins either behavior, so the payload shape can silently flip in later refactors and any consumer relying on the key's absence is bitten.

[ADVISORY] The three added tests exercise only the exact-match branch ('example.com' == 'example.com') and the `ends_with?` branch of `website_name`; the `elsif` branch (equal dot-separated label count greater than 2 with matching `[1..-1]`, i.e. 'www.example.com' vs 'forum.example.com') is never executed by any test in the diff. A regression in the elsif's condition or its `[1..-1]` comparison — the most intricate logic in the new method — ships green: subdomain-hosted instances (forum at forums.example.com, website www.example.com) silently fall back to showing the bare host instead of host+path, with no failing test to catch it.

[BUG] `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` assumes every stored website value parses as a URI, but `URI()` rejects values the removed `website.split('/')[2]` handled — a space in the path or a non-ASCII IDN host raises `URI::InvalidURIError`, which the rescue converts into a nil `website_name`. For such stored website values the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` gate hides the entire globe/link line on the profile where the deleted controller code still rendered the host ('例え.jp' for 'https://例え.jp/', 'example.com' for 'http://example.com/foo bar') — a user-visible display regression for legitimately entered websites that no test covers.

[BUG] website_name returns the bare host without the path when the website host is a subdomain of the instance domain (e.g. website http://www.example.com/profile on instance example.com), because the else-branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) and never the reverse, while the mirror case (instance subdomain of website host, tested at spec line 87) does return host+path. Users whose website URL is www.<instance-domain>/... or any subdomain of the forum's own domain keep seeing the host-only label; the PR's 'show complete URL path when domains match' requirement silently excludes this input class even though the symmetric relationship is implemented and tested, so card/profile labels stay inconsistent with the stated UX goal.

[ADVISORY] The three added specs never execute the elsif branch of website_name (equal label counts > 2, the method's own 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case): discourse.org/example.com and forums.example.com/example.com both fall to the else branch (lengths 2 vs 2 fails the >2 guard; 3 vs 2 fails the equality check) and example.com/example.com hits the exact-match branch. A regression in the split('.')[1..-1].join('.') registrable-domain comparison ships with a green suite and silently changes the displayed website name for www-style websites on subdomain-hosted forums.

[ADVISORY] The new website_name attribute is wired into only the profile template; the user card, which renders the same website field from UserCardSerializer (a subclass of UserSerializer that now also emits website_name), is not touched anywhere in this diff. The hover card keeps rendering the website field through its pre-existing markup (raw URL or host-only extraction), so the same field displays differently on card vs profile and the PR's UX requirement is applied to only one of the two surfaces that show it.

[ADVISORY] For scheme-less website values (e.g. 'example.com', the most common user input form for this field), URI(website.to_s).host is nil so website_name returns nil and the profile hides the website block entirely, while include_website_name (website.present?) still emits the attribute as null; no spec case in the diff covers a website value without a scheme. Users who enter their website without http:// get no website displayed at all with no feedback, and API consumers receive website alongside a null website_name; the diff rewrites exactly this path and adds a presence gate that over-promises relative to the nil value, leaving the case both unhandled and unverified.

[ADVISORY] The sibling-subdomain matching branch of website_name (the elsif at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145-147, the 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case) is the only one of the three matching modes with no test in this diff — the added specs pin only equal hosts, parent domains, and unrelated two-label domains, so the elsif's body never executes in the suite. A regression in the elsif's label-count guard or the [1..-1] suffix slice would silently change the displayed link text for every user whose website is a sibling subdomain of the instance host while the full test suite stays green.

[ADVISORY] The domain-matching rule shipped here is broader than the stated 'same as instance domain' requirement and asymmetric with respect to forum placement: for the domain pair {example.com, www.example.com}, a forum at www.example.com with website http://example.com/user yields 'example.com/user' (else-branch ends_with? match) while a forum at example.com with website http://www.example.com/user yields host-only 'www.example.com' (label-count guard skips the elsif and ends_with? fails), and a website that is a subdomain of the instance host (instance example.com, website http://forum.example.com/x) is excluded entirely — none of this boundary is traceable to the stated requirement or pinned by a test. Users linking sibling or child subdomains of the instance's own domain get inconsistent, placement-dependent display, and future maintainers have no test or stated rule defining the intended boundary, so any refactor of this conditional can silently flip either direction.

[ADVISORY] The new `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` error path for unparseable website values is never exercised by any test in this diff, even though website is user-entered free text and the inline rescue is the load-bearing guard keeping profile and user-card serialization from raising. A later cleanup that drops the rescue turns every user with a malformed website field (e.g. a value with a space or missing scheme) into a 500 on profile and user-card payloads with no failing test, and today the same path already produces the untested payload shape website_name: null with include_website_name true.

[BUG] ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8 resolves conditional attributes via a method named include_<attr>?, so include_website_name (no trailing ?) is never consulted and website_name is serialized unconditionally. Every UserSerializer-derived payload (profile page JSON, user card JSON) for a user without a website carries "website_name": null instead of omitting the key; the gating method the author wrote is dead code, so the intended conditional contract is silently not implemented.

[BUG] The same-site heuristic is asymmetric: when the website host is a subdomain of the instance host (forum at example.com, website http://forum.example.com/bio) the else branch's ends_with? check fails and the path is never appended, while the mirror case (forum at forums.example.com, website example.com/bio) does append it. On forums served from an apex domain, users linking to subdomain pages of the same organization get the bare hostname with no path, even though the diff's own branch-2 comment ('www.example.com == forum.example.com') and its third test treat same-registrable-domain hosts as the same site; different-depth subdomain pairs (a.b.example.com vs forum.example.com) fall through the same way.

[ADVISORY] The host equality and ends_with? comparisons are case-sensitive while URI() preserves the case typed into the website field and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase, so a website entered as http://Example.com/bio never matches example.com. For users who enter mixed-case website URLs the feature silently does nothing (bare host shown, no path appended); the form that is stored/entered and the form that is compared disagree on canonical case, so the next person debugging 'why is the path missing' has no signal.

[ADVISORY] The new branch-2 comparison (equal label counts greater than 2, comparing everything after the first label) is exercised by none of the added specs, which cover only branch 1 (equal hosts), else-true (website is parent of instance) and else-false (unrelated hosts). A regression in the www.example.com == forum.example.com path — e.g., inverting the [1..-1] comparison or dropping the > 2 guard — would ship with the test suite green.

[BUG] The implementation shows the complete URL path for domains that are NOT the same as the instance domain — sibling subdomains (elsif branch) and parent domains (else branch) — silently broadening the stated objective "show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain" into "same registrable domain" without that expansion being part of the accepted intent. Websites on sibling subdomains of a shared multi-tenant domain (e.g., https://team2.herokuapp.com/app viewed on an instance at team1.herokuapp.com, where the two subdomains belong to unrelated parties) display the full path where the announced intent specifies host-only display; the shipped behavior exceeds the objective recorded in the PR title, and no explicit acceptance of the broadened rule is reflected anywhere outside this same PR.

[BUG] Replacing the old split-based host extraction (website.split("/")[2]) with URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil silently regresses website values that URI.parse rejects (e.g., containing a space or raw non-ASCII): website_name returns nil and the template's {{#if model.website_name}} hides the entire globe+link block, where the old code displayed the host. A user whose website field is e.g. 'http://example.com/a b' or 'https://例え.jp' loses their website display on the profile entirely (old behavior showed 'example.com' / '例え.jp'); this display removal for unrelated domains is a behavior change the stated objective never proposed, affecting legacy stored profile data with no code-path trigger in the intent itself.

[ADVISORY] The else branch only handles the website-is-parent-of-instance direction, so a website that is a subdomain of the instance's host (www.example.com/user on instance example.com) gets host-only display while the mirrored configuration (example.com/user on instance www.example.com) gets the full path — inconsistent behavior for symmetric inputs. Users linking a subdomain of the forum's own domain see the shortened form while the reverse configuration shows the full path; the next maintainer extending the matching logic must reason about three asymmetric branches instead of a single same-site predicate, making the inevitable follow-up change ('also treat www.instance as same site') riskier.

[ADVISORY] The three new tests cover exact match, parent-of-instance, and unrelated domains, but no test in the diff exercises the elsif sibling-subdomain branch of website_name (e.g., website www.example.com against instance forum.example.com) in either its positive or negative form. A regression in the suffix comparison in user_serializer.rb line 146 (e.g., comparing full hosts instead of suffixes, or dropping the split('.').length > 2 guard) ships silently and changes the displayed name for every sibling-domain website with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The three new website_name examples never trigger the serializer's elsif branch (user_serializer.rb:144-146, the equal-label-count >2 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case): 'discourse.org' and 'forums.example.com' both fall through to the else branch and 'example.com' takes the equal-hosts branch, so that branch of the new comparison logic ships with zero coverage. A regression in the suffix comparison website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') (an off-by-one or a broken join) passes the full suite green and silently reverts the sibling-subdomain UX this PR introduces to host-only display, with no CI signal.

[ADVISORY] No test exercises the nil-host path of website_name: the only test file in this diff (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb) uses the single well-formed absolute URL 'http://example.com/user' in every example, so `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` yielding nil and the `return if website_host.nil?` early return are never executed by the suite. Users whose freeform website field is unparseable by URI (e.g. contains spaces or unencoded characters) take this path in production; a later refactor that drops the `rescue nil` makes UserSerializer raise URI::InvalidURIError and 500 every profile/card serialization for those users, with no failing test to catch it.

[BUG] For any stored website value that URI.parse rejects (e.g. 'http://example.com/my path' with a space, or an unescaped IDN host like 'https://例え.jp'), `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` silently yields nil and website_name serializes as null, so the template's new `{{#if model.website_name}}` guard hides the entire website entry — whereas the removed client code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still rendered the host for exactly these values. Users whose profile website contains characters the strict URI parser rejects lose their website link from the profile page entirely, with no error, log, or API signal (website is still returned, website_name is just null), so the regression is invisible to both the user and debugging.

[BUG] The equal-label-count suffix heuristic treats any two 3-label hosts sharing the last two labels as the same site, so on an instance at bar.co.uk a website of http://foo.co.uk/x hits `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` ('co.uk' == 'co.uk') and returns 'foo.co.uk/x' — unrelated registrable domains under 2-part public suffixes (co.uk, com.au, co.jp) get the full-path treatment the feature reserves for the same domain. On instances hosted under multi-part public suffixes, external unrelated websites are displayed as if they were internal same-site links (host plus path shown), contradicting the feature's stated contract; display-only since the href is unchanged, but the misfire is silent and untested.

[ADVISORY] The child-subdomain direction is unreachable: a website of http://www.example.com/profile on an instance at example.com fails the equal-label-count branch (3 vs 2) and then `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is false, so the path is hidden — while the mirror-image parent case (website example.com on instance forums.example.com) does show the path, as the new spec encodes. The most common same-site shape (a www.-prefixed URL for the instance's own domain) silently keeps the old host-only display, so the feature applies inconsistently across users of the same instance and the next change to this matcher has to rediscover the asymmetry.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

The added specs only cover non-empty `website` and don’t assert omission vs `null`, so this can slip through.

However, the diff does not show what inputs are allowed/stored for `user_profile.website` (validation/normalization is outside the shown changes), so it’s not verifiable that such values can be “legitimately entered” or exist in practice; it’s a concrete edge-case risk introduced by the stricter parsing and missing coverage rather than a definitively proven regression from the diff alone.

This is an asymmetry vs the handled/tested case where the instance is a subdomain of the website host (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`) and does return `host + path`. However, the diff doesn’t establish a hard correctness requirement that subdomains of the instance domain must also include the path, so this is best framed as an unhandled edge-case / incomplete logic rather than a definite bug.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` will be `nil` for scheme-less values like `"example.com/user"` (Ruby treats it as a path), causing `website_name` to return `nil` early. However `include_website_name` is gated only by `website.present?`, so the serializer will still emit `website_name: null` when a website string exists but has no URI host. The template now keys display off `model.website_name`, so this case remains unhandled and is not covered by the added specs (all test inputs include `http://`). The added specs only cover three scenarios (unrelated domain, exact match, instance subdomain of website host) and do not pin these other boundary cases, so the intended rule is not fully specified/tested even though the code behavior is complex.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The same-site heuristic is asymmetric: when the website host is a subdomain of the instance host (forum at example.com, website http://forum.example.com/bio) the else branch's ends_with? check fails and the path is never appended, while the mirror case (forum at forums.example.com, website example.com/bio) does append it. On forums served from an apex domain, users linking to subdomain pages of the same organization get the bare hostname with no path, even though the diff's own branch-2 comment ('www.example.com == forum.example.com') and its third test treat same-registrable-domain hosts as the same site; different-depth subdomain pairs (a.b.example.com vs forum.example.com) fall through the same way.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the final `else` only appends the path when the *instance* host is a subdomain of the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`), e.g. `forums.example.com` with website `example.com/user`. For the mirror case where the website host is a subdomain of the instance host (instance `example.com`, website `forum.example.com/user`), this condition is false and the method returns just `website_host` without `URI(...).path`. The diff’s logic/comments cover same-host and same-registrable-domain cases, but this asymmetric subdomain direction falls through, producing inconsistent `website_name` output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host equality and ends_with? comparisons are case-sensitive while URI() preserves the case typed into the website field and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase, so a website entered as http://Example.com/bio never matches example.com. For users who enter mixed-case website URLs the feature silently does nothing (bare host shown, no path appended); the form that is stored/entered and the form that is compared disagree on canonical case, so the next person debugging 'why is the path missing' has no signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show case-sensitive string comparisons in `website_name` (e.g., `website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?`), but the finding’s core claim—“URI() preserves the case typed into the website field”—is not verifiable from the diff. The serializer extracts `website_host` via `URI(website.to_s).host`, and whether that retains or normalizes case is a property of Ruby’s URI implementation, not something shown or changed here. Without evidence in the diff that `website_host` can be mixed-case, the asserted mismatch/bug cannot be confirmed from the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new branch-2 comparison (equal label counts greater than 2, comparing everything after the first label) is exercised by none of the added specs, which cover only branch 1 (equal hosts), else-true (website is parent of instance) and else-false (unrelated hosts). A regression in the www.example.com == forum.example.com path — e.g., inverting the [1..-1] comparison or dropping the > 2 guard — would ship with the test suite green.

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` adds a distinct branch for same label-count hosts with >2 labels (the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` case, intended for `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The added specs in `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` cover only: exact host match (`example.com`), unrelated host (`discourse.org`), and instance subdomain where website is parent (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`)—all of which bypass that `elsif`. So a regression inside the `[1..-1]` tail comparison or the `> 2` guard would not be caught by the current tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The implementation shows the complete URL path for domains that are NOT the same as the instance domain — sibling subdomains (elsif branch) and parent domains (else branch) — silently broadening the stated objective "show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain" into "same registrable domain" without that expansion being part of the accepted intent. Websites on sibling subdomains of a shared multi-tenant domain (e.g., https://team2.herokuapp.com/app viewed on an instance at team1.herokuapp.com, where the two subdomains belong to unrelated parties) display the full path where the announced intent specifies host-only display; the shipped behavior exceeds the objective recorded in the PR title, and no explicit acceptance of the broadened rule is reflected anywhere outside this same PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s Ruby serializer deliberately appends the URL path not only when `website_host == discourse_host` but also when hosts share a parent/suffix: in the `elsif` branch it appends the path for “sibling subdomains” when `website_host.split('.')[1..] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..]` (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), and in the `else` branch it appends the path when `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (e.g., `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). This makes the finding’s described broadening/edge case (e.g., multi-tenant `team1.herokuapp.com` vs `team2.herokuapp.com` would also match the `elsif` condition) verifiable from the code, but whether that is a 'bug' depends on intent not present in the diff (the diff even adds a test explicitly expecting path inclusion for the parent-domain case).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Replacing the old split-based host extraction (website.split("/")[2]) with URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil silently regresses website values that URI.parse rejects (e.g., containing a space or raw non-ASCII): website_name returns nil and the template's {{#if model.website_name}} hides the entire globe+link block, where the old code displayed the host. A user whose website field is e.g. 'http://example.com/a b' or 'https://例え.jp' loses their website display on the profile entirely (old behavior showed 'example.com' / '例え.jp'); this display removal for unrelated domains is a behavior change the stated objective never proposed, affecting legacy stored profile data with no code-path trigger in the intent itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the displayed website label from a JS `split("/")[2]` computation to a server-side `website_name` derived via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and updates the template to render the whole globe/link block only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`). In `UserSerializer#website_name`, any `URI` parse failure yields `website_host = nil` and returns, so `website_name` becomes nil even when `website` is present (`include_website_name` checks only `website.present?`). This creates a real behavior change where malformed-but-previously-displayable values (e.g., containing spaces or other characters `URI()` rejects) will cause the website section to disappear entirely, unlike the prior split-based logic which would still often extract a host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The else branch only handles the website-is-parent-of-instance direction, so a website that is a subdomain of the instance's host (www.example.com/user on instance example.com) gets host-only display while the mirrored configuration (example.com/user on instance www.example.com) gets the full path — inconsistent behavior for symmetric inputs. Users linking a subdomain of the forum's own domain see the shortened form while the reverse configuration shows the full path; the next maintainer extending the matching logic must reason about three asymmetric branches instead of a single same-site predicate, making the inevitable follow-up change ('also treat www.instance as same site') riskier.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the final `else` only treats the case where the *instance* host is a subdomain of the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`), returning `website_host + path` (e.g. instance `forums.example.com`, website `example.com/user`). There is no symmetric handling for the opposite direction (website host is a subdomain of instance host, e.g. instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com/user`), which falls through to returning just `website_host` (host-only). This creates the inconsistency described, and the added specs cover only the parent-of-instance direction, not the subdomain-of-instance direction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The three new tests cover exact match, parent-of-instance, and unrelated domains, but no test in the diff exercises the elsif sibling-subdomain branch of website_name (e.g., website www.example.com against instance forum.example.com) in either its positive or negative form. A regression in the suffix comparison in user_serializer.rb line 146 (e.g., comparing full hosts instead of suffixes, or dropping the split('.').length > 2 guard) ships silently and changes the displayed name for every sibling-domain website with no failing test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` with three cases: exact host match, an `elsif` for “sibling subdomains” (same segment count and >2, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), and an `else` for parent/other comparisons. The added specs exercise unrelated domains (`discourse.org`), exact match (`example.com`), and parent-of-instance (`forums.example.com` ends_with? `.example.com`), but do not hit the `elsif` sibling-subdomain branch in either its true or false outcome. That leaves the suffix-comparison logic in that branch untested, as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The three new website_name examples never trigger the serializer's elsif branch (user_serializer.rb:144-146, the equal-label-count >2 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case): 'discourse.org' and 'forums.example.com' both fall through to the else branch and 'example.com' takes the equal-hosts branch, so that branch of the new comparison logic ships with zero coverage. A regression in the suffix comparison website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') (an off-by-one or a broken join) passes the full suite green and silently reverts the sibling-subdomain UX this PR introduces to host-only display, with no CI signal.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, the new `website_name` logic has a distinct `elsif` branch for the “same label count and >2” sibling-subdomain case (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, lines with `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and `> 2`). The added specs only stub `current_hostname` to `discourse.org` (2 labels → falls to `else`), `example.com` (hits the `website_host == discourse_host` branch), and `forums.example.com` (3 vs 2 labels → falls to `else`). None of these can execute the `elsif` branch, so that path ships without coverage as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test exercises the nil-host path of website_name: the only test file in this diff (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb) uses the single well-formed absolute URL 'http://example.com/user' in every example, so `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` yielding nil and the `return if website_host.nil?` early return are never executed by the suite. Users whose freeform website field is unparseable by URI (e.g. contains spaces or unencoded characters) take this path in production; a later refactor that drops the `rescue nil` makes UserSerializer raise URI::InvalidURIError and 500 every profile/card serialization for those users, with no failing test to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` in `UserSerializer` with `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and `return if website_host.nil?`, but the only added/modified specs set `user.user_profile.website = 'http://example.com/user'` and assert behavior for different `Discourse.current_hostname` values. No test case provides an unparseable/relative/invalid website value that would make `URI(...).host` nil or raise (covered by `rescue nil`), so the early-return path is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] For any stored website value that URI.parse rejects (e.g. 'http://example.com/my path' with a space, or an unescaped IDN host like 'https://例え.jp'), `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` silently yields nil and website_name serializes as null, so the template's new `{{#if model.website_name}}` guard hides the entire website entry — whereas the removed client code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still rendered the host for exactly these values. Users whose profile website contains characters the strict URI parser rejects lose their website link from the profile page entirely, with no error, log, or API signal (website is still returned, website_name is just null), so the regression is invisible to both the user and debugging.

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves website display logic from a permissive client-side `website.split("/")[2]` to server-side `website_name` derived via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` (user_serializer.rb). The template now guards rendering on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (user.hbs). If `URI()` raises for an “invalid” but stored website string (e.g. contains spaces or unescaped IDN), `website_host` becomes nil and `website_name` serializes as null while `website` is still present (include_website_name only checks `website.present?`). This makes the website link disappear with no signal, a behavior regression introduced by the new guard + strict parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The equal-label-count suffix heuristic treats any two 3-label hosts sharing the last two labels as the same site, so on an instance at bar.co.uk a website of http://foo.co.uk/x hits `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` ('co.uk' == 'co.uk') and returns 'foo.co.uk/x' — unrelated registrable domains under 2-part public suffixes (co.uk, com.au, co.jp) get the full-path treatment the feature reserves for the same domain. On instances hosted under multi-part public suffixes, external unrelated websites are displayed as if they were internal same-site links (host plus path shown), contradicting the feature's stated contract; display-only since the href is unchanged, but the misfire is silent and untested.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the branch meant for sibling subdomains (`elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`) compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`. For 3-label hosts under a 2-part public suffix (e.g., `bar.co.uk` vs `foo.co.uk`), both sides become `co.uk`, so the code incorrectly treats them as the “same site” case and returns `website_host + path` (e.g., `foo.co.uk/x`). This behavior is directly implied by the diff and is not covered by the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The child-subdomain direction is unreachable: a website of http://www.example.com/profile on an instance at example.com fails the equal-label-count branch (3 vs 2) and then `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is false, so the path is hidden — while the mirror-image parent case (website example.com on instance forums.example.com) does show the path, as the new spec encodes. The most common same-site shape (a www.-prefixed URL for the instance's own domain) silently keeps the old host-only display, so the feature applies inconsistently across users of the same instance and the next change to this matcher has to rediscover the asymmetry.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “same-site” path-including logic only triggers when `website_host == discourse_host`, when both hosts have the same number of dot-labels (>2) and share the same suffix, or when the instance host ends with ".#{website_host}" (website is a parent of the instance). For an instance at `example.com` and a website at `www.example.com`, the equal-label-count branch is skipped (3 != 2) and the final `ends_with?("." << website_host)` check is false (`example.com` does not end with `.www.example.com`), so it falls back to returning only `website_host` (hiding the path). This asymmetry is directly implied by the diff’s logic/comments and is not covered by the added specs.
